fix(hooks): repair red main after the argv normalization, and state the anchor `gh` prerequisite (#1212)

* fix(hooks): keep a subshell cd unmodelable after the argv normalization

origin/main is red: `test_cross_boundary_preflight.sh` fails 2 of 127. The
cause is an interaction between two changes that were each green alone.

#1193 taught the shared `filter_argv` to skip a lone grouping token, so
`( cd B && gh issue create …` now yields argv `['cd', 'B']`. #1148's
`_cd_intent` reads argv to decide whether a chdir is modelable, and that argv
is indistinguishable from a plain `cd B` — so the segment stopped being
opaque and started resolving against B. A subshell's directory change does
not outlive the `)`, so this authorizes the write against a repo it may never
run in, which is the wrong-repo approval the repo-less arm exists to prevent.

`_cd_intent` now tests the UNFILTERED segment for a bare grouping token. The
test sits after the chdir-word check, so a grouped segment that changes no
directory is untouched and still names its resolved repo.

Two rows added pinning that control direction, plus `run_case_detail_absent`
for the assertion it needs — a gate that fires with the wrong reason is a
regression `run_case_detail` cannot see, because a missing needle and a
missing ask look identical to it.

Verified: 127/127 in the hook suite, `./scripts/run-tests.sh` exit 0.
Mutation — impl reverted to origin/main with the tests kept — fails exactly
the 2 original rows; the 2 new control rows pass under it, as a control must.

Refs #1193, #1148

* docs(hooks): state that anchor revision requires gh

The anchor convention is "one comment per PR, edited in place by comment id".
Creating one needs only a way to post a comment; every revision is a PATCH
against the comment id, which needs `gh`. A session whose only GitHub surface
is the MCP server can create an anchor and then cannot revise it — comment
bodies are add-only there, while issue and PR bodies both have update paths.
GitHub REST exposes the PATCH, so the limit is what the host surfaces.

The same absence removes the PostToolUse re-check for a second, independent
reason: that step re-checks structure keyed on `<summary>`, and the MCP read
path strips `<details>`/`<summary>` while keeping the inner text, so a
well-formed anchor read back over it reports as missing every toggle.

PR #1149's anchor was stale for exactly this reason. The precondition was
nowhere in the spec or the Prerequisites table, so a session could enter a
state where the mandated procedure was unperformable with nothing saying so.

Records the precondition and what to do instead in a gh-less session: say so
on the PR and carry the gaps in the PR body or merge commit, rather than
posting a second anchor — a second anchor-shaped comment makes the id-recovery
lookup in "Coupled constant" ambiguous.

Options (b) a real MCP fallback convention and (c) hook-side detection stay
open on #1211; both need their own design review, and (b) needs a survey of
the other gh-less hosts this repo packages for.

Refs #1211, #1149

* docs(hooks): scope the tag-stripping note to comment bodies, not the server

The previous wording said "the MCP read path strips <details>/<summary>",
which invites the wrong conclusion — that the server mangles markup and the
right response is to route around it.

Measured: file contents come back with both tags intact. get_file_contents on
this spec at refs/heads/main returns its own <details> and <summary> verbatim,
matching what git holds. The same session reading a comment body through
pull_request_read or issue_read drops both and keeps the inner text.

So the boundary is content class, not markup: body text a commenter authors is
unfolded, files a reader is meant to trust are not. That is the
prompt-injection boundary drawn deliberately, and it matters for what comes
next — a fallback convention has to survive the unfolding rather than try to
recover the tags.

Refs #1211
